title: Incident triage pocket guide + log translation
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact first-responder pocket guide for security engineers who get paged for incidents that touch RBAC, audit logs, or cross-service SIEM exports. Designed to be low-friction: copy/paste commands, quick decision trees, and a short mapping table that translates noisy logs into probable cause hypotheses.

Intended users:
- Oncall security engineers (first 15–60 minutes)
- SRE/infra engineers assisting with evidence collection
- Incident commanders who need a boiled-down view to decide escalation

High-level triage sequence (first 15 minutes)
1) Confirm scope & blast radius
   - Which service alerted? (auth, api-gateway, console, dedicated-serving)
   - Are there any customer-facing errors or legal/regulatory scopes? If yes, notify CS/Legal immediately (see escalation matrix).
2) Preserve volatile evidence
   - Snapshot processes for affected hosts (ps aux or equivalent).
   - For GPU-hosted nodes, copy /var/log/redwood/runtime.log and the latest 2x kernel logs to a secured bucket (use evidence-s3-write role).
3) Lock down access vectors (short-lived mitigation)
   - If suspect is an account compromise: rotate tokens for affected service account and block suspicious IPs at the edge WAF for 15 minutes.
   - For RBAC-scope issues: temporarily reduce the changed role to read-only while investigation proceeds.
4) Start continuous capture to SIEM
   - Ensure the SIEM export connector is healthy (siem-export health check: /ops/siem/health). If not, trigger the local collector (collector-restart.sh) and mark in ticket.

Evidence capture checklist (commands to run)
- export INCIDENT_ID=<jira or inc id>
- mkdir /tmp/$INCIDENT_ID && cd /tmp/$INCIDENT_ID
- journalctl -u redwood-runtime -S "-30m" > runtime-last-30m.log || tail -n 500 /var/log/redwood/runtime.log > runtime-sample.log
- sudo ss -tunp | tee net-connections.txt
- ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -n 40 > top-procs.txt
- iptables-save > iptables-before.txt (or cloud-network security-group snapshot)
- AWS: aws s3 cp runtime-last-30m.log s3://redwood-evidence/$INCIDENT_ID/ --acl private --profile evidence-uploader
Note: Evidence files must be uploaded under the incident-specific path and labeled with collector name and timestamp.

Minimal chain-of-custody notes (what to write in ticket)
- Who collected: <name/email>
- Hostname/instance-id
- UTC timestamps for each file transfer
- MD5/SHA256 of key evidence files (quick compute)
- Brief description of why file was collected (e.g., failed login spike correlated to 10.1.2.3)

Quick RBAC v2 triage heuristics- "Permission spike" (many grant events in short time): likely admin API key misuse or automation bug. Check /audit/roles/events and correlate on principal_id and request_ip.
- "Unexpected allow": find the audit entry with allow=true and examine the policy_version field and role_binding id (often reveals a recent grant).
- "Service principal anomaly": if service_principal shows a new machine id, search provisioning logs (k8s-controller / infra-provisioning) for the corresponding PR/automation run.

Audit log schema translation table (common fields -> human meaning)
- timestamp -> event time (UTC)
- principal_id -> who performed the action (user/service)
- principal_type -> user | service | infra-automation
- action -> API call or console action (e.g., iam.role.bind)
- target -> resource acted on (role id, dataset id, instance id)
- allow/deny -> policy decision
- policy_version -> which RBAC policy was evaluated (important for rollbacks)
- request_ip -> source IP (map to geolocation and ASN)
- request_id -> trace id (useful to link other logs)

Common SIEM export pitfalls to check quickly
- Missing fields: older collectors sometimes omit policy_version or principal_type. If missing, pull raw node logs instead.
- Timestamps inconsistent: ensure exporter timezone is set to UTC; if not, adjust when correlating across services.
- Sampling applied: some high-throughput services sample audit lines; check exporter sampling flag in header.

Evidence automation quick-hacks
- If evidence automation failed (exporter stopped), default to manual capture and tag with "auto-fail" in ticket.
- Restart commands: systemctl restart redwood-siem-collector || /usr/local/bin/collector-restart.sh --force.
- If automation is partially healthy, enable additional debug level for 15 minutes to get full payloads, then revert.

Decision matrix (escalation triggers)
- Escalate to Incident Commander (SRE lead + Security lead) if any of:
   - Sensitive data exfiltration suspected (PII/PCI/Secrets)
   - Multiple privileged role grants outside of change window (>3 grants/5m)
   - Evidence of lateral movement across VPCs
- Pager duty to Product + CS when customer data or SLA impact is possible.

Short reporting template (copy into Jira/INC)
- Summary (1 sentence): what happened, host/service affected, immediate impact
- Timeline: bullets with UTC timestamps
- Actions taken: bullets (containment, evidence captured, mitigations)
- Next steps + owners
- Short list of artifacts (paths in S3 or ticket attachments)

Outstanding questions / TODOs (for post-incident)
- Can the SIEM exporter include policy_version as a mandatory field? (owner: Marco)
- Add automated MD5 annotation to evidence-s3 uploads (owner: Priya)

References and quick links
- Incident runbook: https://confluence.redwood/company/security/incident-runbook (main runbook)
- RBAC v2 design doc: https://confluence.redwood/company/security/rbac-v2-design
- SIEM export health dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/siem/exports

Notes to self / quick tips:
- Keep responses short on Slack during triage. Use the ticket as the single source of truth.
- If a human-created role-binding looks suspicious, look for recent runbook steps and associated PRs before assuming lateral movement (there are many legitimate infra-automation windows).
- When in doubt: contain (least-impactful action) -> capture -> escalate.

Appendix: brief sample audit log entry and translation
raw log (json-like): {"timestamp": "2025-02-01T14:12:22Z", "principal_id": "svc-build-42", "action": "iam.role.bind", "target": "role:deployers", "allow": true, "policy_version": "v2.1", "request_ip": "18.205.32.10", "request_id": "trc-99a"}
translation: 2025-02-01 14:12:22 UTC — service account svc-build-42 successfully bound role deployers (policy v2.1) from IP 18.205.32.10. Check provisioning jobs around trc-99a.

-- end --

(If helpful, can expand into a one-page printable pdf or add CLI helper scripts to /ops/tools/evidence-helpers.)
